overall: The AG found the November 4, 2013 notice and the visitor comment policy did not violate the Open Meeting Law, offered guidance on the sufficiency of three sets of minutes, and declined to review the later slander/naming allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee manipulated the November 4, 2013 notice, which listed a dinosaur-statue permission vote, to avoid public comment on the project.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the description of this topic was sufficient for members of the public to understand that the Committee would be continuing its discussion of the Dinosaurs Make Cents project.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the visitor comment policy, requiring requests one week before a meeting, violates the law because notice need only be posted 48 hours ahead.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, public bodies have discretion to formulate policies regarding the administration of public comment periods.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by the complainant; the AG reviewed the 2012 and 2013 minutes on its own and found them lacking detail and exhibit listings, offering guidance only.
allegations.key_passage: We remind the Committee that the Open Meeting Law requires that minutes include a sufficiently detailed summary of the discussion that occurred and a listing of all documents and exhibits used during the meeting.

allegations.summary: A later complaint alleged the November 4 minutes named the complainant and slandered her; the AG declined to review because it was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review these allegations because they were not included
